sara: Heads-up — planning a maintenance window for apac1 interruptible GPU cohort to apply NIC microcode + BMC soft-reset. Window: Thu 02:00–06:00 UTC. Impact: only interruptible/spot nodes targeted, but we expect ~10–15% effective capacity loss in APAC during window. Plan below, comments appreciated.

sara: Plan (high-level):
- Cohort approach: 3 racks at a time, rolling across 12 racks (max 1 rack simultaneously).
- Prefer cordon+evict for interruptible nodes only; avoid touching dedicated pools.
- Scheduler mitigation: temporarily shift fairness weights away from short-lived spot jobs to reduce churn (see command snippet).
- Backfill: spin minimal warm-capacity in eu/apac warm-pool for latency-sensitive canaries.
- Observability: pre-run evictions probe and enable extra sampling for 1h pre/post window.

ash: one more detail — we'll lower preemption aggressiveness by reducing preempt_score threshold to 0.5 for the window.

mike: How many active long-running user jobs will be affected? Any dedicated customers at risk? Also cost for warm-pool spinup?

sara: Good q. We ran a census: ~420 active spot pods on target racks, ~14 long-running (checkpointed) jobs flagged as non-preemptible — we'll migrate those to eu-backfill via scheduler hints ahead of time. Dedicated customers: none on those racks (we validated reservations). Warm-pool cost estimate: ~$2.3/hr for minimal backfill (4 gpus) — worst-case $9–10 for the window.

ash: Suggestion — instead of full cordon for a rack, we can try a phased eviction: cordon -> reduce fairness weight -> wait 10m -> drain. That reduces mass evictions and gives headroom for long tasks to checkpoint.

tim: Reminder: add preemption hook to trigger checkpoint for jobs that support it. Example preempt hook call:
```
curl -X POST https://hooks.internal/checkpoint -d '{"job_id":"$JOBID","reason":"maintenance"}'
```
If the job doesn't ack in 60s, we force-evict.

sara: We'll wire that in. Updated sequence:
1) Adjust scheduler weights: `schedulerctl set-weight apac1-interruptible 0.4` (from 1.0).
2) Wait 10m for scheduler to rebalance.
3) For each rack:
   - `kubectl cordon node/<node>`
   - call preempt hook on running pods
   - wait up to 3m for checkpoints
   - `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120` (only on interruptible nodes)
   - BMC soft-reset and NIC microcode apply
   - uncordon
4) Monitor eviction rate and CPU/GPU utilization. Auto-rollback weights on >8% unexpected error.

deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance job created: `maint/apac1-nic-bmc-1748273625`. Runbook: https://internal.runbooks/maint/apac1-2024-11

oncall-bot: Oncall notified. Alert threshold set: evictions > 5% sustained for 10m -> page oncall.

ops-runbooks: Runbook snippet pasted in case anyone needs quick ops steps:
```
# quick checklist
- preflight: ensure eu-backfill warm-pool health
- run: adjust scheduler weight
- per-rack: cordon -> preempt-hook -> drain -> apply fw -> uncordon
- post: revert weights, run smoke tests, validate latency percentiles
```

mike: Any chance we can run this later in the night in APAC local time to reduce customer impact? Thu 02:00–06:00 UTC is 11:00–15:00 JST — a bit rough.

sara: We're constrained by firmware vendor availability and their maintenance maintenance blackout. We can shift 2 hours earlier (00:00–04:00 UTC) but that pushes into US late-evening. I'll run availability poll with vendor and dedicated ops; will update in 2h.

ash: Also: consider a temporary admission-control to cap new spot job admission to 60% during the window. That reduces churn and queue thrashing.

sara: Good call — adding `admissionctl set-capacity apac1-spot 0.6` to sequence.

mike: Cost note: warm-pool + potential re-schedules might add ~0.1% to monthly infra spend if repeated monthly. Fine vs risk.

sara: TL;DR: proceeding with rolling, interruptible-only maintenance with scheduler fairness shift + preempt hooks + minimal warm-pool backfill. I'll post a final comms + precise per-rack timeline after vendor confirms times. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
